resources.string: Choose where the app reads your Nightscout data from. What you enter is stored encrypted on this phone.
Enter the address of the MongoDB database your Nightscout uses. A read-only database user is enough.
No glucose entries found. Check the database name.
Synced. Asked for %4$d stretches of time and checked %1$d readings, %2$d treatments and %3$d insulin-on-board records. Only missing or recent data is requested.
Set up the Nightscout connection on the Connection tab, then sync.
Less than 70%% of readings are available for this period, so these numbers may not represent it well.
No readings in this period. Sync to load them.

Save everything this app holds (the connection and all stored readings) to one encrypted file, and restore it later, for example after reinstalling. Keep the file somewhere safe, and remember the passphrase: it cannot be recovered. Restoring adds readings and never deletes any.
At least %1$d characters. Needed to restore.
Backup saved. %1$d readings and the connection are in it.
The saved connection was restored. Check it on the Connection tab.
The backup had no connection, so the current one was kept.
No treatments in this period. Sync to load them.
%1$d meals, %2$s g carbs per day on average
Bolus insulin %1$s U in total, %2$s U per day (includes automatic micro-boluses, not basal)
Only %1$d days of data (at least %2$d needed), so no pattern is shown.
Meals are carb entries of 5 g or more, with entries within 30 minutes merged. Meals eaten while glucose was already low are left out.
Only %1$d meals (at least %2$d needed), so no pattern is shown.
Above range 2 hours after: %1$d of %2$d meals
Low within 4 hours after: %1$d of %2$d meals
No readings in this period. Sync to load them.
This is right now. Touch and slide a finger across the chart to see any earlier moment.
No glucose reading near this time
No basal information for this time
Last 3 hours: %1$s g carbs, %2$s U bolus
Part of this period has not been synced yet. Press Sync now to fill it in; only the missing part is requested.
No insulin-on-board data for this time
Nightscout returned nothing for these days

How often the closed loop ran a higher or lower basal than your profile schedule, from the temp basals it set. Percentages are of the time a temp basal was running. The baseline is the profile that was in force at each moment, including any percentage and time shift (AAPS switch records).
Loop data covers %1$s%% of this period.
Loop data covers only %1$s%% of this period (temp basals are missing for the rest), so these numbers describe part of it.
Basal insulin per day: %1$s U vs %2$s U on profile
%1$d temp basals (%2$s a day): %3$d above, %4$d below, %5$d at profile when set
Mark a day as bad data, for example when a pump failed and you used insulin pens. Excluded days are left out of Autotune and of the Patterns tab, and they are kept in your backup.
Total basal per day: %1$s U before, %2$s U after

Profile switches and logged site, insulin and sensor changes, only those with enough glucose on both sides to compare, newest first and one card per day (the day\'s latest change, with any others that day named in the title). Each shows up to 7 days of glucose either side, stopping at the neighbouring change. This shows what happened, not why: meals, illness and activity differ between weeks.
No profile, site, insulin or sensor changes in this period have enough glucose on both sides to compare (at least 2 days each side).

Every profile configuration that took effect, newest first, with the glucose it saw while it was in force. If a newer one did worse, open the older one to read its settings back. Edits made in one day count as one configuration.
Not enough glucose recorded while it was in force.
This record does not carry sensitivity or carb ratio.
%1$d of %2$d days had enough data and were used.
Autotune uses one value for the whole day, so these are daily averages of your profile.
Low confidence means few days, or hours with little usable data that were filled in from their neighbours.
Held at the current rate. Autotune wanted %1$s U/h, but %2$s.
Reads from your Nightscout site over the internet, a little at a time. No database address is needed. Your saved MongoDB connection is kept untouched and can be switched back to at any time.
Insulin type (sets the peak activity time)
%1$d days have glucose but no insulin records

No boluses and no loop temp basals were recorded on these days, so the pump was probably off or had failed and insulin went unrecorded (for example pens). Their glucose says nothing about basal or sensitivity. Autotune already skips them; excluding them also removes them from the Patterns tab.
Based on %1$d meals and %2$d insulin-only readings.
That is little data: treat the carb ratio and sensitivity as low confidence.
Choose how many days to replay and press Run. Only days with insulin records are used.
Only days run on your current profile are used: it last changed on %1$s. Days before that are skipped, so applying a result and re-running does not move the values on again from old data.
Syncing the latest data first. Run autotune when it finishes.
